patterns: Show your tools: Pınar's 'my favorite pens' photo did ~21k views and 321 saves on about 1.1k followers, two days after her October drawing roundup. A plain photo of the things you actually use gets saved, not just liked.
One-line design opinion: Craig Mod's whispered 'the industrial design team was absolutely correct' hit ~222k. A short, confident aside about a made object travels when the image does the explaining.

Reading journal vs. margins: several small accounts asked whether people annotate their books or keep a separate reading journal, and the questions pulled replies on tiny follower counts. It is a live, friendly argument on her topic.
Paper planner season: an author ordering her 2027 paper planner and asking who else still uses one got 23 replies. Late October is when planner people start talking.

Mental health told as one sentence someone said: the burnout post built around a psychologist's line, and the therapist-journal posts, use a single remembered sentence as the hook. Few replies yet, so there's room.
Skip: Yongfook's SaaS posts and Vassallo's trades-vs-doctors take are big but off-brand. Awais Aftab's suicidality excerpt is important reading and not a place to reply with a brand.

reply_ideas.description: Belgian storyteller on burnout and anxiety, and the line his psychologist gave him: the more attention you give something, the more it grows
reply_ideas.reply_text: I like that he didn't tell you to win the argument with your own head. Letting a thought pass sounds simple until it's two in the morning and it won't leave. Did he give you anything to do in those moments, or did it mostly take practice?

reply_ideas.description: author and fiction editor Karin Beery just ordered her 2027 paper planner and asked who else still uses one
reply_ideas.reply_text: I'm curious whether a fiction editor's planner ends up looking like a manuscript by March, with notes in the margins and things crossed out. Do you buy the same one every year, or is picking it part of the fun?

reply_ideas.description: actor and vocalist who went to the Toronto Pen Show for one hour and came out a fountain pen person
reply_ideas.reply_text: An hour is plenty of time for that to happen, honestly. What did you come home with, and have you picked a first ink yet or are you still staring at the bottles?

video_tip: 15 seconds, no face. Overhead on textured cream paper, a hand sets down the few pens it actually uses, worn caps and all, then picks one and writes a single line. Paper and nib sounds only, no music. End on a card that reads 'Which pen do you actually reach for?' Pairs with the favorite-pens post.
